session_policy.reason: It develops a missing negative and reuses a valid negative; spk_render explicitly forces redevelopment.
session_policy.ownership: Caller frees JSON with spk_string_free, results with spk_result_free, sessions with spk_session_release before engine_destroy.

region_exposure_peaks.input: Every source pixel, after fixed source colour/WB/exposure preparation; no preview sampling; auto_exposure=false
region_exposure_peaks.measurement: frame_exposure_peak is the maximum after scene latitude, spectral reconstruction and camera exposure; frame_boosted_peak is its exact GPU boost result before clipped-highlight headroom
region_exposure_peaks.execution: For bounded source regions, reduce both fields across non-overlapping source strips and send the same pair on every render region. No prepass when boost and headroom are both off.
region_exposure_peaks.default: Both fields default to -1 and retain the original full-frame device reductions. These transient execution fields are not user settings.

product_mapping.grain_particle_area_um2: max(1e-6, .8*grain_size^2*style_area_scale); strength never changes spatial pitch
product_mapping.grain_texture: 1=fine,2=classic,3=coarse,4=clustered; 0 preserves the upstream Poisson sublayer path
product_mapping.black_and_white: Real spectral emulsion + silver density and Ilford paper, DIR disabled; neutral CMY=[0,0,68].
product_mapping.extensions: Retain independently calibrated neutral CMY and illuminant only for matching calibrated paper; DIR and scanner black/white correction disabled.

limits.raw_headroom: This boundary accepts float32, but the current LibRaw RGB16 source remains display-referred and does not restore unclipped RAW highlights.
limits.reference_parity: Full C++/Vulkan spectral model; not claimed byte-identical to historical Python model, nor C1/LR rendering.
limits.android: Android JNI builds the same pipeline with bounded region IO. Physical pixel pitch and composed spatial halo must be retained. Tiled random grain is statistically consistent, not a whole-frame byte-equivalence claim.
